units.title: Sensors
units.blurb: Encoders, sound echoes and inertial sensors.

units.title: Noise and Estimation
units.blurb: Averages, filters and the Kalman filter's idea: blend a prediction with a measurement.

topics.title: Wheel Encoders
topics.short: Counts divided by counts per turn give turns; turns times the circumference give distance.
topics.trouble: Students use the radius instead of the circumference, or forget the gear ratio between motor and wheel.

topics.title: Ultrasonic Distance
topics.short: Sound goes out and back, so distance = speed of sound times time, divided by 2.
topics.trouble: Students forget to halve the round trip.

topics.title: Accelerometers and Gyros
topics.short: At rest, an accelerometer's tilt is atan(ax / az); a gyro gives turn rate, which adds up to angle and drifts.
topics.trouble: Students trust the accelerometer while the robot is speeding up, or the gyro's angle after a long time.

topics.title: Noise and Averages
topics.short: Averaging N independent readings shrinks the noise by the square root of N.
topics.trouble: Students expect averaging 4 readings to cut the noise to a quarter, not a half.

topics.title: The Complementary Filter
topics.short: Trust the gyro over short times and the accelerometer over long times: θ = α(θ + ω Δt) + (1 − α) θ_acc.
topics.trouble: Students swap the weights and trust the noisy accelerometer most.

topics.title: A Kalman Filter in One Dimension
topics.short: Gain K = P / (P + R); new estimate = old + K (measurement − old); new P = (1 − K) P.
topics.trouble: Students think a Kalman filter just averages; it weighs each source by how much it is trusted.
